title: Dago on the dark side of indie life: exits, passive income myths and overworking
summary: Dago launches the new This Indie Life format with Nico, focused on the unglamorous side of bootstrapping. He shares lessons from his failed logo startup, why passive income is a myth, why indies should plan an exit, and how overwork and success highs derail founders.

principles.text: Social media's success-only feed makes founders feel like failures, so share the hard parts honestly.
principles.quote: when you open social media and only see success at least for me I start to feel like a failure real fast

principles.text: Don't over-invest in quality for a market that won't pay for it; match effort to what buyers actually value.
principles.quote: mistake we did is we went after a market that is like doesn't have much money and like we went at it with like highest quality like every logo is designed by hand

principles.text: Passive income is a myth: earning without working demands huge active effort first.
principles.quote: it's so active like it's the opposite it's active income like it takes so much work to make money without working

principles.text: Avoid emotional attachment to your company and plan an exit if you want to stay indie.
principles.quote: I think now at least if you want to stay Indie you need to plan an exit

principles.text: If sustaining the business requires extreme hours for years, the product itself may be wrong.
principles.quote: if you need to work this hard for this long maybe it's the wrong product you know

principles.text: Success highs breed overconfidence; keep doing the things that brought you the win.
principles.quote: when you get the high you can make mistakes because now because you're high on like the success
